title: Shared grammar compiler scaling and representational bounds
status: Prepared local compiler-only prerequisite; not pushed or submitted

sources.contribution: Shared rule FSM storage, packed-row reachability, and one per-grammar productivity table; scaling tests
Fallible grammar optimization and FSM representation guards; grammar-memory accounting; configurable compiler size cap; golden-mask and oversized-input tests

extraction: Exact crates/xgrammar path delta from the Atlas base through the second source commit. No scheduler, GLM model, kernel, server policy, or GPU changes.
behavior: Share complete FSM storage across rule views instead of cloning it.
Build and reuse grammar productivity metadata; walk packed FSM rows directly.
Reject grammar rule counts and bounded repetition indices that cannot be represented by i16 FSM edges.
Expose a configurable compiled schema size limit, checked before cache insertion; preserve the compiler default of usize::MAX.
Include rule views, state maps, and productivity metadata in memory accounting. This makes existing byte-budget eviction more accurate.
deferred: The server 1 MiB schema text limit, 64 MiB compiled-schema limit, and 512 MiB grammar cache budget are not included. Upstream server settings remain unchanged.

HTTP 400 propagation, strict response_format enforcement, and compiler panic containment from the integrated branch are not included. Base Atlas compile_grammar_state falls back to unconstrained generation on compilation errors; this prerequisite does not repair that existing behavior.
The GLM-specific grammar state and speculative scheduler changes remain in the later GLM integration.
No GPU behavior or GLM runtime qualification is claimed for this compiler-only extraction.
Attribution does not establish additional contributor CLA or commercial relicensing rights.
